catalog_citation: Moñino, Yves. 1995. Le proto-gbaya: essai de linguistique comparative historique sur vingt-et-une langues d'Afrique centrale (SELAF 357; Langues et cultures africaines 20). Paris/Louvain: Peeters. xiv+725 pp.
catalog_locator: p. 285, 'Récapitulation contrastive', Remarque 2, directly under the table of tonal-modification areas a1-a4 whose row a3 reads 'kara, lai, toongo'; second sentence p. 345, 'Correspondances phoniques', Remarque.
catalog_quote: Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). [p. 345, Remarque:] On pourrait poser que la langue ancestrale ne connaissait que des syllabes ouvertes et un accent : *CV, *CVCV (qui aurait donné CVCV non accentué) et *CVCV (qui aurait donné CVC). L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution.
world_status: statement found in a copy we already had

new_statements.translation: Remark 2. To the question raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them currently shows any phenomenon of accent, intensity or length. The hypothesis will be raised again in diachrony, in interpreting the sound correspondences (p. 345). [p. 345:] The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not force this solution for proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis is conceivable at an earlier stage of the evolution.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Northwest Gbaya (Kara/'bodoe, Lai) is a tone language (two levels, four tones H, L, LH, HL per Roulon-Doko 2025) and, per Moñino, has no accent, no intensity (stress) and no length phenomenon at all; tone alone is the word-prosodic system.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the denial covers all 21 languages surveyed. Older sources use an accent mark ad hoc: Naumann 1915 (Bouar dialect) '´ bezeichnet die Betonung einer Silbe' and Hartmann 1930 'besondere Betonung einer Silbe ist durch einen Akzent angegeben (ndía)', without any placement rule; Tucker & Bryan 1966 §2b note only 'a tendency towards extra shortness' on the penult in GBAYA.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, in the context of tonal modification of lexical tone schemes in syntagms; not a citation-form statement. Roulon-Doko 2025 (Negation in Northwest Gbaya, HAL) and all other open Roulon-Doko items downloaded describe tone only and are silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding statement (Moñino 1995: 285, Remarque 2) is a comparative statement covering all 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka languages surveyed; the table it annotates lists 'kara, lai' (row a3), which Glottolog maps to Northwest Gbaya [gya] (Moñino 1995 language code: 'Gbaya du Nord (quatre parlers Kara / deux yaayuwee)', 'Gbaya Lai'). Moñino's own primary field language is gbaya 'bodoe, a Kara variety (pp. 51-52), so it is a first-hand claim for nort2775 but formulated at the group level. No open copy of the dedicated descriptions (Moñino & Roulon 1972; Noss 1981 [Yaayuwee]; Roulon-Doko 1997) could be reached.
